summary: alelo-services exfiltrates environment variables and credential files on npm install
details: The package's preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts in index.js collect the installer's full process.env plus hostname, username, platform, and cwd, and additionally read local secret files (.env,.npmrc,../.env,../../.env) whose contents commonly include npm auth tokens, CI tokens, and cloud credentials. The collected data is POSTed via https.request to the hardcoded endpoint alelo1786663101.requestcatcher.com at paths /preinstall and /postinstall. Both hooks fire automatically on `npm install`, so any developer or CI machine that installs this package leaks its environment secrets and dotfile contents to an anonymous public request-inspection bucket. A bundled login.ps1 references a local publish workflow and the account oxy12@proton.me, consistent with a hit-and-run credential-harvest package rather than a legitimate service library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
